headline: Approved up to $2,000,000 in bonds for Four Hills Landfill, $575,000 for road salt, and nine fleet vehicle and equipment purchases.
summary: Nine Fleet Department vehicle and equipment purchases were approved, along with a $575,000 order of winter road salt. Three Hazen and Sawyer wastewater contracts were also approved, including a $270,626.25 capacity analysis. Hardship requests to excavate on Brook Street, Garden Street, and Patten Court during paving moratoriums also passed.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the September 24, 2026 meeting, unanimously.
Approved R-26-062, authorizing bonds not to exceed $2,000,000 for Four Hills Landfill improvements, unanimously.
Approved the wastewater user warrants as presented, unanimously.
Approved a contract with Hazen and Sawyer of up to $108,871.66 for a toxicity study at the wastewater treatment facility, unanimously.
Approved a contract with Hazen and Sawyer of up to $145,778. 31 for a local limits evaluation at the wastewater treatment facility, unanimously.
Approved a contract with Hazen and Sawyer of up to $270,626.25 for a capacity analysis at the wastewater treatment facility, unanimously.
Approved Change Order #1 of $217,600.00 to install a splash pad at Jeff Morin Park, pending CBDG funds, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of winter road salt for $575,000.00 from Granite State Minerals and Eastern Minerals, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of a 2026 Kenworth T280 service truck for $256,373.00, plus a radio and up-fit not to exceed $5,000.00, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of two 2027 Freightliner cab and chassis trucks for $325,308.00 each, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of a 2027 Ford F-350 pickup truck for $97,376.00, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of a 300-P-Tier John Deere excavator for $395,000.00, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of three Load Master rear load waste collection vehicles for $361,629.37 each, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of two 2027 Ford F-250 plow trucks for $63,505.00 each, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of a Whittke front loader waste collection vehicle for $624,963.80, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of a 2027 Ford F-250 pickup truck with plow package for $65,481.00, unanimously.
Approved the purchase of two 2027 Ford F-250 pickup trucks for $60,975.00 each, unanimously.
Approved the creation of an additional Solid Waste Assistant position at $28.26 an hour, unanimously.
Approved Change Order #2 with Core and Main, not to exceed $10,000.00, for landfill waterline and hydrants, unanimously.
Approved a contract amendment with SCS Engineers through June 30, 2030, with a revised amount of $38,320.00, unanimously.
Approved an amendment with Sanborn Head & Associates, not to exceed $57,500.00, for PFAS testing near the Nashua Fire Training Center, unanimously.
Approved the sewer service permits and fees as submitted, unanimously.
Approved a drainlayer’s license for White Mountain Excavation, LLC of Candia, New Hampshire, unanimously.
Approved a drainlayer’s license for D & S Excavating, LLC of Weare, New Hampshire, unanimously.
Approved appraisal services by Bergeron Commercial Appraisal, not to exceed $54,000.00, for the Walnut Street Oval project, unanimously.
Approved Change Order No. 2 with RWC Enterprises, not to exceed $172,350.00, for the 2026 sewer and drain improvement project, unanimously.
Approved a contract with ADS, LLC of Huntsville, Alabama for $25,000.00 for a sewer and drain flow monitoring system, unanimously.
Approved, unanimously, a motion to consider the hardship request from John and Cheryl Morin to excavate and install utilities on Brook Street.
Approved, unanimously, a motion to consider the hardship request from Greenman-Pedersen for Nashua Parking Services to excavate and install utilities on Garden Street.
Approved, unanimously, a motion to consider the hardship request from Pennichuck Water Works to excavate and install a water main in Patten Court.
Accepted the retirement of Paul Haskell, park foreman, effective October 30, 2026, unanimously.
Accepted the resignation of Tim Gaumond, streets operator, effective October 9, 2026, unanimously.
Approved and unsealed the non-public personnel minutes from September 24, 2026, unanimously.
Approved, by roll call of 4-0, sealing the minutes of the October 22, 2026 non-public personnel session until a majority votes otherwise.

Motion by Commissioner Espitia: To Approve The Contract With Hazen And Sawyer Of 
Boston, Massachusetts  In An Amount Not To Exceed $108,871.66, For A Toxicity Identification 
And Reduction Evaluation For The Effluent At The Wastewater Treatment Facility.  Funding Will 
Be Through: Department: 169 Wastewater; Fund: Wastewater; Activity: Inflow Infiltration.   
 
David Boucher, Superintendent, Wastewater Department 
 
Thank you, Dave Boucher, Wastewater Superintendent.  The wastewater facility is required to 
hold effluent toxicity sampling periodically under our EPA issued permit.  Because we failed 
multiple times, the new permit that issued to us this year requires us to do a toxicity 
identification and toxicity reduction analysis.  What this does is it looks at our facility, and it 
identifies what the toxicity--what's causing the toxicity at the facility.  It will also help identify the 
corrective actions to reduce or eliminate that toxicity at the facility.  I would like to use Haze and 
Sawyer, they have a familiarity with the facility, and they also have expertise in this field doing 
this kind of study.  I'd be happy to answer any questions.   
 
Vice-Chairman, Gregg 
 
Open up for questions.   
 
Commissioner, June Lemen 
 
What happens if they can't figure out what is causing this problem?  I mean, I understand that 
this is a requirement from EPA, so I assume there is some kind of fallback if they can't figure it 
out or are we just going to assume that they will be able to figure out whatever this is?   
 
Mr. Boucher 
 
I'm assuming that they'll figure it out.  We have to do a lot of sampling in the facility and recreate 
that failure, and I'm sure we'll be able to.  But with that, we think it may be within the facility.  It 
might be on the outside of the facility that's causing it.  That's what it is going to determine, and 
then there'll be a corrective action plan to address it.
_____________________________________________________________________________________________

Okay, thank you.

Yeah, my question would be would this company also look at just storm drains?  Because I 
know in some areas of the City there's no connected--we have the two systems, so that will also 
be looked at?   
 
Mr. Boucher 
 
This study will look at inside the facility, as what's causing it inside the facility.  If it stems to the 
outside, then yes, we will be looking outside and doing sampling.  Looking at what might be 
entering catch basins is needed, but first we'll be looking at industries that could be-- depending 
on what it is.  If they're targeted industries or maybe not.  Right now we don’t know what's 
causing it, so we don’t know which direction to look.   
 
Mr. O'Brien 
 
Yeah, because I was looking at maybe some industry may be still tied into our system.   
 
Mr. Boucher 
 
Right.

questions?   
 
Commissioner Paul Shea 
 
Is this tied to the outlet that we talked about at the last meeting?  Where the water kind of 
bubbles up out of the, from underneath to the river surface?   
 
Mr. Boucher 
 
The testing that kind of initiated this whole study is our discharge limit, which is the effluent just 
before it goes to the river.  So, it's the testing that we do just prior to it going to the river is what 
is failing.   
 
Commissioner Shea

Thank you.

Motion by Commissioner Shea: To Approve The Contract With Hazen And Sawyer Of 
Boston, Massachusetts, In An Amount Not To Exceed $145,778. 31, For A Local Limits 
Evaluation At The Wastewater Treatment Facility.   Funding Will Be Through: Department: 169 
Wastewater; Fund: Wastewater; Activity: Inflow Infiltration.   
 
David Boucher, Superintendent, Wastewater Department 
 
David Boucher, Wastewater Superintendent.  The local limits are limits that are developed by 
the municipality for the industrial users.  This is designed to protect the wastewater facility from 
receiving anything it shouldn't.  Mostly things like heavy metals, sulfates, things of that nature, 
so we give them limits.  Our new permit requires that we do an evaluation of these local limits.  
The last time it was done, a full-blown study was done, was 1992, so we're due.  We do check it 
annually to make sure that the numbers that we have are sufficient, but the new permit is 
requiring us to do this full-blown study.  Again, this is something we'd like Hazen and Sawyer to 
do because of their familiarity, and this also ties in to some of the other studies we have going 
on.   
 
Vice-Chairman Gregg 
 
Okay, any questions?   
 
MOTION CARRIED: Unanimously.   
 
 D. Motion: To Approve The Contract With Hazen And Sawyer Of Boston, 
Massachusetts, In An Amount Not To Exceed $270,626.25 For A Capacity Analysis At The 
Wastewater Treatment Facility.  Funding Will Be Through: Department: 169 Wastewater; Fund: 
Wastewater; Activity: Capacity Analysis.
_____________________________________________________________________________________________
Board of Public Works Meeting of October 22, 2026  Page 6 of 40 
Vice-Chairman, Matthew Gregg 
 
Item D. Commissioner Espitia.   
 
Motion by Commissioner Espitia: To Approve The Contract With Hazen And Sawyer Of 
Boston, Massachusetts, In An Amount Not To Exceed $270,626.25 For A Capacity Analysis At 
The Wastewater Treatment Facility.  Funding Will Be Through: Department: 169 Wastewater; 
Fund: Wastewater; Activity: Capacity Analysis.   
 
David Boucher, Superintendent, Wastewater Department 
 
David Boucher, Wastewater Superintendent.  We've been observing some changes in the 
characteristics of the wastewater--the water pulling into the wastewater facility.  The strength of 
it.  It's also affecting some of the process, and it goes back to some of our evaluations that we're 
doing.  Plus, we've seen growth in the City; more flow, changes in, we're seeing an uptake in 
ammonia, stuff like that, so it's important that we do a capacity analysis.  This would take place 
inside the facility and may extend to the outside of the facility as well.  This study is to identify 
existing and potential process constraints that we have inside the facility.  It will also help give 
us the ability to accommodate future projects or projected flows coming to the facility with all the 
new housing developments that are coming, and if we have to build any new processes we can 
also add that to our future long-terms of the facility.  This would help us identify those things.  
Again, we'd like to have Hazen and Sawyer do this as this ties into the other two projects, and 
we do have some cost savings with that with the sampling and some of the existing documents 
that they have to review.  I'd be happy to answer questions.   
 
Vice-Chairman Gregg 
 
Any questions?   
 
Michael B. O'Brien, Sr., Board of Aldermen 
 
I would just like to say, I would be interested when this report comes, and being Chairman of 
Infrastructure, we've got new developments.  I don't know if we can or can't, but maybe if it's 
going to cause us upgrading our existing system, maybe we can talk to developers and see if 
any contributions can be made for the upgrades.  We'll have to see.  See what the report says.   
 
Mr. Boucher 
 
Makes sense.   
 
Vice-Chairman Gregg 
 
Any other?  Hearing none.  Okay.   
 
Commissioner Manny Espitia 
 
Doing any major—I know obviously we're doing this proactively, but have you seen any major 
issues given—we had like that rainstorm that was a long rainstorm for three days.  Just like with 
the change of weather, any main issue?  And the growing population in the City.  Any real 
issues that I think could affect us at the wastewater plant?
_____________________________________________________________________________________________

One of the things we do see, and there is kind of--I don't know if it's coincidence the correlation 
is that we've seen a lot of population growth, a lot of housing growth and all that, but we've been 
doing a lot of lining of the sewer pipes and eliminating a lot of the water that's coming in through 
broken pipes.  It's kind of balancing out the flows, but we're starting to see an increase of 
ammonia coming into the facility.  Ammonia is natural coming from households, and so it's more 
concentrated.  It seems we had the dilution coming in from cracks and pipes helped, but now 
that we're not seeing that, we're just seeing more concentrated ammonia.  That's one of the 
things we're looking at.   
 
Mr. Boucher 
 
Thank you.

Motion by Commissioner Lemen: To Approve The Change Order #1 Of The Wading Pool

Bryan Conant, Superintendent, Parks and Recreation 
 
Good evening, Bryan Conant, Superintendent of the Parks Department.  This is going to be to 
install the splash pad features we've already purchased in Jeff Morin Park.  The old Park Social.  
This is going to greatly enhance the park.  We've also got plans that you've approved a

_____________________________________________________________________________________________

Mr. Conant 
 
Yes.  Thank you, Director Fauteux.  I'm pretty sure the CBDG funding won't be available until

Vice-Chairman, Gregg 
 
Questions?

How much salt is this?

For tonnage?
